explanation: The curves intersect where x²+x−2=0, giving x=−2 and x=1. The enclosed region has −2≤x≤1 and −2≤y≤2. Rectangles I and III contain it completely; II excludes points above y=1, including (0,2).

source_feedback_interpretation.source_problem:
Let $D$ be a finite region enclosed by the curves $y=-{x}^{2}+2$ and $y=x.$ If 

$$
f(x,y)={\begin{aligned}{x}^{3}-xy, & (x,y)\in R\cap D \\ 0, & (x,y)\in R∖D\end{aligned}\,\text{and}\,{∬}_{D}({x}^{3}-xy)\text{d}A={∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A,
$$

which of the following could be the definition of the rectangular domain $R?$

- $R=[-2,1]\times [-2,2]$
- $R=[-2,2]\times [-2,1]$
- $R=[-2,2]\times [-2,2]$
source_feedback_interpretation.interpreted_problem:
Let $D$ be a finite region enclosed by the curves $y=-{x}^{2}+2$ and $y=x.$ If 

$$
f(x,y)={\begin{aligned}{x}^{3}-xy, & (x,y)\in R\cap D \\ 0, & (x,y)\in R∖D\end{aligned}\,\text{and}\,{∬}_{D}({x}^{3}-xy)\text{d}A={∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A,
$$

Require $D\subseteq R$, so the rectangle contains the entire region. Which of the following could be the definition of the rectangular domain $R?$

- $R=[-2,1]\times [-2,2]$
- $R=[-2,2]\times [-2,1]$
- $R=[-2,2]\times [-2,2]$
source_feedback_interpretation.confidence_scope: Mathematical validity for the explicitly containing rectangle request; the original equality alone can admit other choices by cancellation.
